courses.name: Application of AI in Business
courses.description:
This course explores the applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in different business domains, including
marketing, finance, strategy, operations, human resources, Equity, Diversity, Inclusion and Indigeneity (EDII),
sustainability, and product development. Additionally, the course introduces AI tools and their practical
applications across these domains.
courses.courseOutline:
• Introduction to AI in Business
• AI in Marketing and Customer Engagement
• AI in Finance and Investment
• AI in Human Resources and Talent Management
• AI in Operations and Supply Chain
• AI in Business Strategy
• AI and Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Indigeneity (EDII)
• AI and Sustainability
• AI in Product Development and Innovation
• Final Project and Future Trends

learningOutcomes.text: Evaluate and critically analyze real-world AI applications in business, considering ethical considerations such as bias, transparency, and privacy
Apply AI techniques and tools to solve current business challenges
Develop skills for continuously monitoring and adapting to evolving AI trends and technologies
Apply the mindset of an entrepreneur and assess one’s own potential of becoming an entrepreneur.
Develop and assess business ideas based on the opportunity and industry analysis, problem-solution and product-market fit based on the value proposition.
Evaluate the financing, legal, intellectual property & regulatory compliance aspects of starting a business.
Develop skills in "pitching" a business idea clearly and concisely to the stakeholders.
Develop an ethical and sustainable business plan that adheres to EDII concepts.

courses.name: Entrepreneurship
courses.courseOutline:
• Entrepreneurship, entrepreneurs and managers, Innovators and entrepreneurs, Disruptive innovations
• Business Model Canvas, Lean Canvas, and Competitive analysis, Business Idea Journal, Building team
• Recognize opportunity, Value Proposition Canvas, Customer Segmentation
• Customer discovery interview, HADI cycle, Product-Solution fit
• Elevator pitch, Building a business plan
• Mullin’s model framework, VRIO analysis, marketing channel, Website marketing, social media, and 
guerrilla marketing
• Business Model Canvas, Cost Structure, Key Resources, Activities, and Partners
• Revenue models, Financial projections, and Pricing strategy
• Sustainability, Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Indigenization considerations in entrepreneurship
• Bootstrapping, Crowdfunding, Angel investors, Venture Investors, Governmental incentives
• Legal aspects of founding the company, Patents, Copyrights, Trademarks
• Exit strategy, Final Pitch of the Business Idea.
courses.description:
This course introduces students to the process of creating their own business venture from opportunity 
recognition, idea generation and customer discovery, towards the launch of their innovative business. The 
course investigates the main challenges associated with the first steps of startup. Students assess the 
opportunities, build, and verify business hypothesis, define the right customer segments, market research, and 
plan strategic development of their brand-new venture. Various frameworks are introduced that can help them 
start a new venture as they further explore the legal aspects and the fundraising process. Upon the completion 
of the course, students will have the capacity to reasonably assess the problem-solution and product-market fit 
and how to pitch their ideas to investors.
